articles.title: Who Is Anupama Ramachandran? The Chennai Cueist Who Became the First Indian Woman to Win a World Snooker Title — and Just Defended It at Home
articles.excerpt: Born in Chennai in 2002, Anupama Ramachandran chose snooker over chess at a Mylapore Club summer camp at 13, won a world under-16 title at 15, and in November 2025 became the first Indian woman to win the IBSF World Snooker Championship — then defended it in Indore on November 21, 2026, to become the first Indian to win back-to-back world snooker crowns, all while completing two postgraduate degrees.
articles.image_caption: Anupama Ramachandran lines up a shot at the snooker table during competition. The Chennai player won her first IBSF world title in Doha in November 2025 and defended the crown in Indore in November 2026.
articles.nri_angle: The Chennai cueist who became the first Indian woman to win a world snooker title — and the first Indian to defend one — gives diaspora fans a new name at the top of a sport India had never conquered, and a visible path for girls who want to follow her to the table.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Who Is Harmanpreet Kaur? The Moga Batter Who Captained India to Its First Women's World Cup — and Just Became the First Female Cricketer Honoured With a Wax Statue
articles.excerpt: Born in Moga, Punjab, Harmanpreet Kaur debuted for India at 20, announced herself with 171 not out in a World Cup semi-final, captained India in 211 internationals to its first Women's World Cup in 2025 — then stepped down in October 2026 and, weeks later, unveiled a wax statue in Jaipur organisers call the world's first of a female cricketer.
articles.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur poses alongside her wax statue at its unveiling in Jaipur on November 13, 2026. Organisers describe the figure, bound for the Historica museum at Nahargarh Fort, as the world's first wax statue of a female cricketer.
articles.nri_angle: The Moga-born all-rounder who became the first Indian woman signed by an overseas franchise — playing in front of diaspora crowds in Australia's Big Bash and England's Hundred — captained India to its first Women's World Cup in 2025 and remains the face diaspora fans associate with the women's game's rise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ares Management Reportedly in Talks for Minority Stake in Kolkata Knight Riders
articles.excerpt: Moneycontrol reporting says the US asset manager is in advanced discussions over about 20% of the IPL franchise from the Mehta Group, at a valuation of over $1.8 billion — with no final agreement reached.
articles.image_caption: The Eden Gardens stadium just before the beginning of the Indian Premier League match between the Kolkata Knight Riders and the Chennai Super Kings, on the 18th of May, 2008. articles.nri_angle: For diaspora fans who watched the 171 and the World Cup run from abroad, the Jaipur statue marks women's cricket's arrival in the same hall of fame long reserved for Tendulkar, Dhoni and Kohli.
